body:
Global crypto markets closed Friday, October 23 in a distinctly defensive posture, with total market cap settling at $2.75T after shedding 2.85% in 24 hours on volume of $68.4B. The mood shifted meaningfully from yesterday: the Fear & Greed index collapsed from 68 (Greed) to 50 (Neutral) in a single session, which is the kind of sentiment whiplash that tends to flush out leveraged longs rather than attract fresh capital. BTC dominance held firm at 59.4%, with ETH dominance at 10.6%, both numbers confirming that when risk appetite contracts in crypto, capital consolidates into bitcoin rather than rotating into the broader market. The session had the character of a controlled pullback rather than a rout, but the altcoin tape told a messier story underneath.

Bitcoin printed $81,505, down 0.36% on the day and 0.64% on the week, but the more important context is the 24-hour volume of $25.51B against a relatively tight intraday range — the market is grinding rather than trending. A CoinDesk headline noted bitcoin "steadies near $81,700" and separately that it is "holding above $81,000 as markets calm," which tells you the $81,000 level is the immediate line in the sand that bulls are defending. The key levels to watch are straightforward: a clean hold above $81,000 keeps the near-term structure intact, while a break below that handle opens the door to a more meaningful test of the mid-$79,000s. To the upside, $83,500-$84,000 is where sellers have shown up twice in the past 10 days. One headline worth flagging: CoinDesk reported that bitcoin "appears to have decoupled from midterm cycle bottom history," which, if accurate, removes one of the cleaner historical timing signals traders have leaned on. Treat that narrative with appropriate skepticism until price confirms.

Ethereum slipped 0.32% to $2,395.21 on volume of $11.6B, underperforming bitcoin on the week at -2.56% versus BTC's -0.64%, a divergence that continues to frustrate ETH holders and reinforces BTC's dominance squeeze. SOL held up comparatively well on the day, off just 0.03% to $104.34, but the weekly print of -2.10% keeps it in the red alongside most of the smart-contract layer. The real standouts in both directions were at the edges of the tracked universe: DOT surged 4.80% to $1.18 on $0.17B in volume, leading the 24-hour board; BNB added 1.65% to $745.57 and is actually positive on the week at +1.94%, a quiet but notable show of relative strength. UNI gained 0.96% to $7.17. On the other side, AVAX continues to be the most painful name in the cohort — down 0.84% today to $9.16 and down a brutal 11.06% on the week, a performance that separates it sharply from peers. ADA's 7-day loss of 6.25% and LINK's -4.44% over the same period round out the altcoin damage. The PEPE mention in a CoinDesk headline (+13% according to that report) is a reminder that speculative appetite hasn't entirely evaporated — it has just retreated to meme-coin pockets where position sizes are smaller.

The macro context is providing no particular tailwind. Oil is continuing to gain according to the market updates headline, which complicates the Fed's inflation calculus and keeps rate-cut expectations under pressure heading into the next FOMC cycle. The significant regulatory and institutional story of the day is HSBC: both CoinDesk and Cointelegraph reported that HSBC has launched a Hong Kong dollar stablecoin for retail payments through its app, reaching over 3 million everyday users, and separately that Malaysia and Thailand have joined Singapore's cross-border stablecoin framework. This is not noise — a G-SIB deploying a retail stablecoin product to millions of customers is a structural development for the asset class, even if price didn't react today. Bybit securing the first full Dubai spot trading license is another piece of the regulatory normalization picture. None of this is moving BTC or ETH on a 24-hour basis, but it is the kind of institutional and jurisdictional foundation-laying that changes the demand structure over quarters, not days.

Looking ahead, the critical near-term variable is whether $81,000 holds into the weekend. Weekend sessions carry thinner books and can amplify moves in either direction, and with sentiment already back to neutral from greed in a single day, the path of least resistance for a momentum-light market is lower until a fresh catalyst appears. Watch U.S. rate expectations for any re-pricing that could pressure risk assets broadly; oil's continued move higher is the macro variable most likely to do that. On the upside, any positive surprise out of Washington on crypto regulation or a macro print that brings rate cuts back into view could snap this range quickly. AVAX needs to stabilize and find a bid or it risks becoming a crowded short and a canary for broader altcoin sentiment. The HSBC stablecoin story and the Southeast Asian cross-border framework are worth monitoring for follow-on adoption announcements that could shift the stablecoin volume narrative. Until BTC reclaims the $83,500 zone with conviction, this market is in a prove-it phase, and discretion beats aggression.
